title: RideLink Value-Added Trips — Summary of Allotments and Destinations
content:
Beyond medical trips, Non-Emergency Medical Transportation carries value-added one-way trips to non-medical destinations on most RideLink levels. This summary lists the yearly allotment, the destinations served, the distance limit and whether the allotment is prorated for a benefit activated after January.

| Level | Value-added one-way trips per benefit year | Destinations served | Longest one-way value-added trip (miles) | Allotment prorated for activation after January |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RideLink Transit Pass | 24 | Pharmacy, WIC, food bank, community health class | 15 | Yes |
| RideLink Mileage Reimbursement | 0 | None | 0 | Yes |
| RideLink Ambulatory Sedan | 24 | Pharmacy, WIC, food bank, community health class | 15 | Yes |
| RideLink Door-to-Door Assist | 24 | Pharmacy, WIC, food bank, community health class | 15 | Yes |
| RideLink Wheelchair Van | 12 | Pharmacy, WIC, food bank, community health class | 15 | Yes |
| RideLink Stretcher Van | 0 | None | 0 | Yes |

## Reading the summary

- RideLink Mileage Reimbursement and RideLink Stretcher Van carry no value-added trips.
- RideLink Wheelchair Van carries 12 trips a year; RideLink Transit Pass, RideLink Ambulatory Sedan and RideLink Door-to-Door Assist carry 24.
- The four destinations are the same on every level that carries trips, and each value-added trip is limited to 15 one-way miles.

*Hypothetical cases:* a 12-mile one-way trip to a food bank is within the 15-mile limit; a 16-mile one-way trip to a community health class is not. A trip to a pharmacy on RideLink Stretcher Van cannot be a value-added trip, because that level carries none.
